Mr. Rahul Jain (Chief Financial Officer, Suzlon Group) | products = [[Wind turbines]][[Renewable energy]] | brands = | production = | production_year = | services = | revenue = {{up}} {{INRConvert|10890|c}} (2025) | operating_income = {{up}} {{INRConvert|1447|c}} (2025) | net_income = {{up}} {{INRConvert|2072|c}} (2025) | assets = {{up}} {{INRConvert|12943|c}} (2025) | equity = {{up}} {{INRConvert|6106|c}} (2025) | owner = Tanti Family | num_members = | num_members_year = | num_employees = 8,500 | num_employees_year = 2026 | parent = | divisions = | subsidiaries = SE Forge | module = | website = {{URL|http://www.suzlon.com}} | footnotes = }} '''Suzlon Energy''' is an Indian [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[wind turbine]] manufacturer headquartered in [[Pune]], [[Western India]]. == History == [[Tulsi Tanti]] was a [[Gujarati people|Gujarati]] businessman managing a small textile company. Due to the erratic availability of local power and its rising cost, the highest business expenditure after the raw materials was electricity.{{cite book |title=[[India's Global Powerhouses]] |last=Kumar |first=Nirmalya |author-link=Nirmalya Kumar |year=2009 |publisher=[[Harvard Business Press]] |isbn=978-1-4221-4762-7 |pages=136–8}}{{cite magazine|url=http://www.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0,28804,1663317_1663322,00.html|title=Heroes of the Environment|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130825150950/http://www.time.com/time/specials/2007/article/0,28804,1663317_1663322,00.html|archive-date=25 August 2013|magazine=Time|date=17 October 2007|access-date=26 December 2009}} Tanti ventured into wind energy production as a way to secure the energy needs for his textile company. After commissioning two wind turbines, Tanti discovered that wind energy was an even better business than textiles and founded Suzlon Energy.{{cite web|title = India's 40 Richest| work=Forbes|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120727215554/http://www.forbes.com/global/2006/1127/039.html|archive-date=27 July 2012|url=https://www.forbes.com/global/2006/1127/039.html |access-date=14 February 2015|date=17 November 2006}} It set up its first manufacturing facility at Diu. In 1996, Suzlon commissioned its first customer wind turbine for Indian Petrochemical Corporation Ltd at Dhank, Gujarat. The wind farm has powered 70,000 households in Gujarat completing over 25 years of operations.{{Cite web|url=http://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/renewable/suzlons-first-wind-farm-completes-20-years-of-operations/53188351|title=Suzlon’s first wind farm completes 20 years of operations|website=ETEnergyworld.com}} Suzlon's technology partner for these earliest projects was German Südwind . In 2000 Suzlon got an order from Tata Finance and its wholly owned subsidiary, Niskalp Investment & Trading, to supply wind turbines for a 60 MW wind power project It setup India's first 1 MW unit at Supa, Ahmednagar in Maharashtra under the order.{{Cite web|url=https://www.windpowermonthly.com/article/960815/indias-first-1-mw-unit-erected|title=India's first 1 MW unit erected}} Suzlon produced first-ever "made-in-India" wind turbine blades, S60, manufactured at its rotor blade unit in Daman in 2002{{Cite web|url=https://www.thewindpower.net/turbine_en_200_suzlon_s60-1000.php|title=Suzlon S60/1000 - Manufacturers and turbines - Online access - The Wind Power|website=www.thewindpower.net}} Suzlon adopted a business model wherein clients would be responsible for 25% of the up-front capital investment and Suzlon would arrange the remaining 75% on loan. Initially, Indian banks were hesitant to fund loans for this model, but by 2008, many Indian banks started financing wind power projects for Suzlon's clients. In 2001, Tanti sold off the textile business and took over as chairman of Suzlon Group. In 2003, Suzlon ventured into international markets with an order from [[DanMar]] to supply 24 turbines in southwestern [[Minnesota]], United States and set up an office in [[Beijing]], China.{{cite news |url=https://www.forbes.com/forbes/2006/0619/124.html |title=Wind Man |work=Forbes|date=27 October 2006 |access-date=22 November 2011 |first=Naazneen |last=Karmali |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120114181600/http://www.forbes.com/forbes/2006/0619/124.html |archive-date=14 January 2012 |url-status=live }} Suzlon Rotor Corporation began producing the blades in [[Pipestone, Minnesota]] in 2006.{{cite web|url=https://www.renewableenergyworld.com/wind-power/story-of-a-windmill/?id=46688|title=Story of a windmill|access-date=1 December 2023|work=Renewable energy world|date=7 October 2010 }} Suzlon reached a definitive agreement for acquisition of [[Belgium|Belgian]] firm [[Hansen Transmissions]], specializing in [[gearboxes]] for wind turbines, for $565 million in 2006 and purchased a controlling stake in Germany's [[Senvion]] valued at US$1.6 billion in 2007. In June 2007, Suzlon had signed a contract with [[Edison Mission Energy]] (EME) of the United States for delivery of 150 wind turbines. In November 2009, the company decided to sell 35% stake of Hansen for $370 million as part of its debt restructuring program and appointed [[Bank of America]] [[Merrill Lynch]] and [[Morgan Stanley]] as the managers and [[bookrunner|book runners]].{{cite news|url=http://www.livemint.com/2010/02/01224856/Suzlon-awaiting-large-orders.html |title=Suzlon: awaiting large orders|work=Livemint|date=2 February 2010 |access-date=22 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100410081226/http://www.livemint.com/2010/02/01224856/Suzlon-awaiting-large-orders.html |archive-date=10 April news|url=http://www.suzlon.com/images/Media_Center_news/198_Press%20Release.pdf|title=Suzlon Press Release|date=14 May 2011|access-date=23 December 2012|work=Suzlon}} In October 2011, Suzlon sold its remaining 26.06% stake in Hansen Transmissions to ZF Friedrichshafen AG for {{INRConvert|8.9|b}}.{{cite news |url=http://mobile.bloomberg.com/news/2011-10-07/suzlon-energy-to-receive-178-million-for-hansen-stake-next-week |title=Suzlon Energy to Receive $178 Million for Hansen Stake Next Week- Bloomberg |url-status=live }} In the same month, it also achieved full control of its German subsidiary REpower Systems (now [[Senvion]]) by acquiring the remaining 5% stake held by minority shareholders for EUR 63 million.{{cite news |last=Yep |first=Eric |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052970203554104577003263853518948 |title=Suzlon: Completed 'Squeeze-Out' Process of REpower Minority {{INRconvert|7200|c}} to reduce the debts.{{cite news|title=Suzlon to sell German unit to Centerbridge for €1 2016|url-status=live}} In a further equity infusion, [[Dilip Shanghvi]], the founder of [[Sun Pharmaceuticals]], agreed to purchase a 23 percent stake in Suzlon for a sum of {{INRconvert|1800|c}}.{{cite news|title=Dilip Shanghvi takes 23 per cent stake in debt-laden Suzlon|url=http://businesstoday.intoday.in/story/dilip-shanghvi-takes-23-per-cent-stake-in-debt-laden-suzlon/1/215732.html|access-date=16 February 2015|work=Business Today|date=14 February 2015}} The deal shrank Tanti's holding to 24 percent, but management control remained with the Tanti family. Its total borrowings stood at {{INRconvert|11430.76|cc}} in FY15-16 from {{INRconvert|17810.96|c}} in FY14-15.{{cite news|url=http://www.indiainfoline.com/article/news-top-story/suzlon-suzlon-to-exit-debt-restructuring-by-end-of-fy17-117010900179_1.html|title=Suzlon {{!}} Suzlon to exit debt restructuring by end of FY17|work=Indiainfoline|access-date=17 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170114203448/http://www.indiainfoline.com/article/news-top-story/suzlon-suzlon-to-exit-debt-restructuring-by-end-of-fy17-117010900179_1.html|archive-date=14 January 2017|url-status=live}} In May 2024, Suzlon secured new orders from [[Juniper Green Energy]] to develop 402 MW wind energy projects in Fatehgarh, Rajasthan. The deal includes installation of 134 wind turbine generators, each with a rated capacity of 3 MW.{{Cite web |title=Suzlon secures Wind Energy Projects from Juniper Green Energy |url=https://themachinemaker.com/news/suzlon-secures-wind-energy-projects-from-juniper-green-energy |access-date=2024-05-26|website=Machine Maker|date=22 May 2024 }} The market capitalization of
